article.headline: Davis and Dybantsa lead the Wizards past the Raptors 103-99 in a matchup of struggling teams
article.description: — Anthony Davis had 25 points and 14 rebounds, rookie AJ Dybantsa added 23 points and 12 boards, and the Washington Wizards beat the undermanned Toronto Raptors 103-99 on Wednesday night to snap an eight-game losing streak.
article.story: TORONTO -- — Anthony Davis had 25 points and 14 rebounds, rookie AJ Dybantsa added 23 points and 12 boards, and the Washington Wizards beat the undermanned Toronto Raptors 103-99 on Wednesday night to snap an eight-game losing streak. Canadian Kyshawn George added 20 points for the Wizards, who got off to a promising 4-3 start but hadn't won since. His 3-pointer with 8:55 left in the fourth capped an 11-0 Wizards run that made it 91-82, Washington's biggest lead to that point of the game. Immanuel Quickley scored 24 points and Jamison Battle added 19, including five 3-pointers, as Toronto lost its sixth straight. RJ Barrett (right hamstring tightness) and Scottie Barnes (left groin injury management) were ruled out for the game hours before tipoff, joining superstar Kawhi Leonard (left knee injury management) on the Raptors’ injury report. Things got worse for Toronto in the second quarter when Collin Murray-Boyles left the game with an undisclosed illness. He had one point, two rebounds and an assist in five minutes of play as the Raptors’ starting power forward. Toronto was a dismal 7 for 14 at the free throw line, struggling for the third game in a row. The Raptors were 10 for 19 (52.6%) in Sunday’s 112-108 loss to the New York Knicks and 10 for 18 (55.6%) on Tuesday in a 111-102 loss to New York. Up next Wizards: Visit the Chicago Bulls on Friday for an NBA Cup game. Raptors: Visit the Detroit Pistons on Friday in an NBA Cup game. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
